extracted.intended_audience: Title IX coordinators, school and college administrators, legal/compliance officers, and other recipients of federal education funding implementing grievance and informal resolution procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of evaluation/implementation criteria from the Department of Education's Title IX final regulations preamble concerning informal resolution (§106.44(k)) and grievance procedures (§106.45, §106.46), including facilitator qualifications, notice requirements, privacy, appropriate resolution methods, and due process safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of potential terms in informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(k)(3)(v): the recipient must provide notice of the potential terms that may be requested or offered in an informal resolution agreement, including notice that an informal resolution agreement is binding only on the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice need not cover every possible measure, remedy, or sanction; it should provide general framework/parameters so parties can give informed consent. Binding-only-on-parties prevents offering unenforceable terms that depend on non-party actions (e.g., requiring a non-party to undergo training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of what information may be maintained or disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(k)(3)(vi): a recipient must explain to the parties what information related to informal resolution it may maintain and whether and how it could disclose such information for use in grievance procedures under §106.45 (and, if applicable, §106.46) if grievance procedures are initiated or resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarification is intended to balance ensuring parties are aware of consequences of informal resolution and providing flexibility to structure informal processes that suit the program or activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with §106.44(j) and limitation on disclosure of personally identifiable information
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must comply with §106.44(j) when conducting an informal resolution process and must not disclose personally identifiable information about the participants except in the circumstances enumerated in that provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a privacy safeguard to limit disclosure of participants' identifying information during or following informal resolution, subject to enumerated exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required description of informal resolution process and right to withdraw
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(k)(3) requires providing parties a description of what the informal resolution process requires, potential terms of any informal resolution agreement, and the right of the parties to withdraw from that process and pursue the recipient's grievance procedures instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notice requirements aim to ensure parties understand contours of the informal process and can make an informed decision whether to choose or continue informal resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitator training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(k)(4) requires that any person facilitating informal resolution must receive training under §106.8(d)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is consistent with research/best practices (e.g., restorative justice implementation) and is intended to ensure facilitators are prepared to conduct appropriate, trauma-informed processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitator impartiality and conflict-of-interest prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(k)(4) requires that any person facilitating informal resolution must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guardrail is intended to protect the integrity of informal resolutions, avoid appearance of bias, and preserve trust in grievance processes should formal procedures be initiated or resumed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on facilitator also serving as investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulation retains the prohibition (as proposed) that the informal resolution facilitator not also serve as the investigator, to guard against appearance of bias or conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although commenters expressed concern about staffing burdens and single-investigator models, the Department declined to modify this because separate roles help ensure fair and reliable outcomes if formal grievance procedures later proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of terms allowed in informal resolution agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(k)(5)(ii) clarifies that parties may agree to informal resolution terms that the recipient could have imposed at the conclusion of a recipient's grievance procedures, including remedies or disciplinary sanctions that the recipient could have imposed upon a determination that sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision uses illustrative, non-exhaustive examples; the Department revised wording for clarity to tie such terms to what could have been imposed 'had the recipient determined at the conclusion of the recipient's grievance procedures that sex discrimination occurred.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on contact may be mutual or non-mutual and may be imposed pre-decisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on contact under §106.44(k)(5)(i) may be mutual or non-mutual. A recipient may impose restrictions on contact prior to completion of grievance procedures either as supportive measures during the pendency of grievance procedures (§106.44(g)(1)) or as a term of an informal resolution agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that recipients are not limited to mutual no-contact orders and may use pre-decisional supportive measures or agreement terms as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parents' and legal representatives' rights in informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in Title IX or these regulations may be read to derogate any legal right of a parent, guardian, or other authorized legal representative to act on behalf of a complainant, respondent, or other person (subject to §106.6(e)), including the right to access documents or information to which they are legally entitled (see §106.6(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should ensure informal resolution processes account for legally recognized parental/guardian rights where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of informal resolution methods (mediation vs restorative practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal resolution may encompass mediation, restorative justice, transformative justice, and other alternative dispute resolution processes; recipients have discretion to choose options best for them, the parties, and their communities. The Department acknowledges mediation may be inappropriate for allegations such as sexual assault and that restorative practices may be more trauma-informed and survivor-centered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may decline to offer mediation if it would be inappropriate; no specific conflict exists between §106.44(k) and restorative/transformative models. The Department will offer technical assistance and may issue guidance on best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline grievance procedures: prompt, equitable, transparent, and fair
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.45 establishes the basic elements of a fair process and sets clear guideposts for prompt and equitable resolution of complaints of sex discrimination (including sex-based harassment) to ensure transparent and reliable outcomes for recipients, students, employees, and others participating or attempting to participate in an education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements are designed to be consistent with due process principles while affording recipients flexibility to tailor procedures to their educational environments; they apply across a range of recipients (elementary, secondary, postsecondary, agencies, libraries, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional procedural protections for postsecondary student-harassment complaints (§106.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.46 (applies to sex-based harassment complaints involving a student at a postsecondary institution) retains and requires additional procedural protections, including opportunity to have an advisor of choice at any meeting or proceeding (§106.46(e)(2)), allowing an advisor to ask relevant (not otherwise impermissible) questions during a live hearing (§106.46(f)(1)(ii)(B)), and appeal opportunities based on procedural irregularity, new evidence, or conflict of interest or bias (and any other equally-offered bases) (§106.46(i)(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.46 also ensures adequate notice and access to evidence (§106.46(c),(d),(e)(1),(e)(5)) and preserves a recipient's authority to prohibit knowingly making false statements; these protections reflect retention of certain 2020 amendments appropriate to postsecondary contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to relevant evidence and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations ensure that complainants and respondents have adequate notice of allegations, dismissals, meetings, interviews, hearings, and delays, and equal opportunity to access relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence (see §106.46(c),(d),(e)(1),(e)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements are intended to provide transparency and permit meaningful participation while preserving limitations on impermissible evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for single-investigator model as a recipient option
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed framework and final rules provide flexibility allowing a recipient to adopt a single-investigator model in appropriate contexts, though commenters asked for guidance on avoiding bias/conflict of interest in such models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognized concerns and suggested use of outside entities may alleviate concerns; however, separate-role guardrails for informal resolution facilitators remain to protect integrity if formal procedures proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process standards vary with context and constitutional constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Due process obligations vary with the circumstances—procedural protections required in criminal or judicial proceedings are not automatically required in all administrative or educational contexts. Public postsecondary institutions are subject to constitutional due process; private institutions are bound by fairness under contract/common law/statute; the Department will not impose procedures that would require recipients to restrict constitutional rights (34 CFR 106.6(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should use context-specific balancing (e.g., Mathews v. Eldridge) to determine what process is due, ensuring procedures comport with relevant constitutional/state/federal legal requirements.
